Name: Climate Change Act 2008
Statutory_Enabling_Basis: Primary Act of Parliament — self-authorising. Grants Ministers power to make secondary legislation including Carbon Budget Orders (s.8), the NAP (s.58), CCRA duties (s.56), and adaptation regulations.
Key_Provisions: Legally binding net-zero GHG target (100% reduction by 2050 vs 1990; amended 2019). Establishes carbon budgets (5-year caps). Creates Climate Change Committee (CCC). Requires National Adaptation Programme (NAP) and Climate Change Risk Assessment (CCRA). Requires government to respond to CCC reports.
Intl_Links: [INT-L-001] UN Framework Convention on Climate Change; [INT-L-002] Kyoto Protocol to the UNFCCC; [INT-L-003] Paris Agreement; [EU-L-005] EU Climate Law (Regulation EU 2021/1119, amended by Regulation EU 2026/667)

Name: Climate Change Act 2008 (2050 Target Amendment) Order 2019
Statutory_Enabling_Basis: Climate Change Act 2008, s.2(1): power to amend the 2050 target percentage. Order made under this section following receipt of CCC advice on net-zero. Affirmative procedure (both Houses).
Key_Provisions: Amends the 2008 Act to replace the previous 80% reduction target with a net-zero target (at least 100% reduction) by 2050. Implements the recommendation of the CCC.

Name: Carbon Budget Orders (1st–7th)
Statutory_Enabling_Basis: Climate Change Act 2008, ss.8–9: duty on SoS to set each carbon budget by Order; Parliament must approve by affirmative resolution. Each Order is laid before Parliament after receipt of CCC recommendation.
Key_Provisions: Secondary legislation setting each 5-year carbon budget: CB1 (2008–12), CB2 (2013–17), CB3 (2018–22), CB4 (2023–27, 1,950 MtCO₂e), CB5 (2028–32, 1,725 MtCO₂e), CB6 (2033–37, 965 MtCO₂e). CB7 (2038–42) advised by CCC in 2025; to be set by statute by June 2026.
Intl_Links: [INT-L-001] UN Framework Convention on Climate Change; [INT-L-002] Kyoto Protocol to the UNFCCC; [INT-L-003] Paris Agreement

Name: Environment Act 2021
Statutory_Enabling_Basis: Primary Act of Parliament — self-authorising. Grants Ministers power to set environmental targets by secondary legislation (s.1), make BNG regulations (Sch.14), establish OEP (Part 2), issue EIP (s.9), and make regulations on Local Nature Recovery Strategies (Part 7).
Key_Provisions: Sets legally binding environmental targets for England (species abundance, habitat creation/restoration, air quality, water). Creates Office for Environmental Protection (OEP). Introduces Environmental Improvement Plan (EIP) duty. Requires Biodiversity Net Gain (BNG) for development. Establishes Local Nature Recovery Strategies (LNRS). Environmental principles policy statement. Duty on public authorities to conserve/enhance biodiversity. [Themes: nature-based solutions; natural capital; ecosystem services]
Intl_Links: [INT-L-004] UN Convention on Biological Diversity; [INT-L-005] Cartagena Protocol on Biosafety; [INT-L-007] Kunming-Montreal Global Biodiversity Framework; [INT-L-022] Aarhus Convention — UN/ECE Convention on Access to Information, Public Participation and Access to Justice in Environmental Matters; [EU-L-021] EU Deforestation Regulation (EUDR, Regulation EU 2023/1115, amended by Regulation EU 2025/2650); [EU-L-022] EU Soil Monitoring Law (Soil Monitoring and Resilience Directive, Directive EU 2025/2360)

Name: Wildlife and Countryside Act 1981
Statutory_Enabling_Basis: Primary Act of Parliament — self-authorising. Section 28 provides powers to designate SSSIs; s.37A enables the Minister to make regulations on species licensing.
Key_Provisions: Primary framework for protection of wild birds, animals and plants. Provides SSSIs designation. Amended by CROW Act 2000, CRoW Act 2000, Natural Environment and Rural Communities Act 2006 etc.
Intl_Links: [INT-L-010] Convention on International Trade in Endangered Species; [INT-L-011] Convention on Migratory Species (CMS / Bonn Convention); [INT-L-012] Bern Convention on European Wildlife and Natural Habitats; [EU-L-002] EU Birds Directive (Directive 2009/147/EC — codification of 79/409/EEC)

Name: Natural Environment and Rural Communities Act 2006 (NERC Act)
Statutory_Enabling_Basis: Primary Act of Parliament — self-authorising. Section 2 establishes Natural England; s.27 establishes JNCC; s.40 imposes biodiversity duty on public authorities.
Key_Provisions: Creates Natural England and dissolves predecessor bodies. Imposes biodiversity duty on public authorities (s.40). Defines purpose of Natural England as conserving, enhancing and managing the natural environment.

Name: Conservation of Habitats and Species Regulations 2017
Statutory_Enabling_Basis: European Communities Act 1972 (now retained EU law via European Union (Withdrawal) Act 2018): instruments originally made to implement EU Habitats and Birds Directives; retained and amended post-Brexit. Specific power preserved under EUWA 2018 s.2.
Key_Provisions: Implements (retained EU) Habitats Directive. Designates Special Areas of Conservation (SACs) and Special Protection Areas (SPAs). Requires Habitat Regulations Assessments. Protects European Protected Species.
Intl_Links: [INT-L-012] Bern Convention on European Wildlife and Natural Habitats; [EU-L-001] EU Habitats Directive (Council Directive 92/43/EEC); [EU-L-002] EU Birds Directive (Directive 2009/147/EC — codification of 79/409/EEC)

Name: Biodiversity Beyond National Jurisdiction Act 2026
Statutory_Enabling_Basis: Primary Act of Parliament — self-authorising. Enables UK to ratify the UN BBNJ Agreement and make implementing regulations under s.9.
Key_Provisions: Enables UK to ratify the UN BBNJ Agreement (High Seas Treaty) on conservation of marine biodiversity in areas beyond national jurisdiction. Covers marine genetic resources, area-based management tools, EIAs on the high seas. Royal Assent Feb 2026.
Intl_Links: [INT-L-004] UN Convention on Biological Diversity; [INT-L-014] UN Convention on the Law of the Sea; [INT-L-015] Agreement on Biodiversity Beyond National Jurisdiction (BBNJ — 'High Seas Treaty'); [INT-P-018] High Seas Alliance / 30×30 for the Ocean

Name: Marine and Coastal Access Act 2009
Statutory_Enabling_Basis: Primary Act of Parliament — self-authorising. Grants powers for marine planning, licensing, conservation zones and coastal access.
Key_Provisions: Creates Marine Management Organisation (MMO). Establishes marine planning system and Marine Conservation Zones (MCZs). Enables UK Marine Policy Statement and marine plans. Creates coastal access rights.
Intl_Links: [INT-L-013] OSPAR Convention for the Protection of the Marine Environment of the North-East Atlantic; [INT-L-014] UN Convention on the Law of the Sea; [INT-L-017] Helsinki Convention (HELCOM) — Baltic Marine Environment Protection Convention; [INT-L-018] London Protocol (Protocol to the Convention on the Prevention of Marine Pollution by Dumping of Wastes); [EU-L-013] EU Maritime Spatial Planning Directive (Directive 2014/89/EU)

Name: Water Industry Act 1991
Statutory_Enabling_Basis: Primary Act of Parliament — self-authorising. Section 2 grants the Secretary of State powers over Ofwat.
Key_Provisions: Regulates appointment and functions of water and sewerage undertakers in England and Wales. Grants Ofwat regulatory and licence enforcement powers. Basis for water company price controls and duty to maintain water supply.

Name: Water (Special Measures) Act 2025
Statutory_Enabling_Basis: Primary Act of Parliament — self-authorising. Creates new powers under Water Industry Act 1991 (as amended) including Ofwat's new duty to contribute to Climate Change Act and Environment Act targets (s.5).
Key_Provisions: Strengthens Ofwat's powers over water companies. Adds new duty for Ofwat to contribute to meeting Environment Act and Climate Change Act targets. Enables criminal liability for water company executives. Gives Secretary of State powers to place companies in special measures.
Intl_Links: [EU-L-017] EU Bathing Water Directive (Directive 2006/7/EC — revision of 76/160/EEC)

Name: Energy Act 2023
Statutory_Enabling_Basis: Primary Act of Parliament — self-authorising. Grants powers for NESO creation, hydrogen licensing regime, CCUS licensing, and heat network zoning by secondary legislation.
Key_Provisions: Creates National Energy System Operator (NESO) as independent body. New licensing for hydrogen and Carbon Capture Utilisation and Storage (CCUS). Expands offshore wind leasing. Establishes heat network zoning. Reforms electricity market for low-carbon energy.
Intl_Links: [EU-L-005] EU Climate Law (Regulation EU 2021/1119, amended by Regulation EU 2026/667); [EU-L-014] EU Emissions Trading System (Directive 2003/87/EC, as amended by Directive EU 2023/959); [EU-L-019] EU Renewable Energy Directive III (Directive EU 2023/2413 — RED III recast); [EU-L-020] EU Energy Efficiency Directive III (Directive EU 2023/1791 — EED III recast)

Name: Electricity Act 1989 (as amended)
Statutory_Enabling_Basis: Primary Act of Parliament — self-authorising. Grants licensing and market intervention powers for electricity generation and supply; amended by later Energy Acts.
Key_Provisions: Core electricity licensing framework. Amended by Energy Acts and Contracts for Difference (CfD) regime under Energy Act 2013 to support renewable deployment.

Name: Planning and Infrastructure Act 2025
Policy_Sector: Nature & Biodiversity | Urban & Buildings | Land Use & Agriculture | Climate | Transport
Statutory_Enabling_Basis: Bill before Parliament — no statutory basis yet. Intended enabling powers for Nature Restoration Fund, Environmental Delivery Plans and planning reform derived from Planning and Compulsory Purchase Act 2004 powers and new primary legislation.
Key_Provisions: Wide-ranging planning and infrastructure reform. Part 3 (development and nature recovery) introduces Environmental Delivery Plans [POL-037] and the Nature Restoration Fund / Levy [POL-038], administered by Natural England, as an alternative route for developers to discharge specified environmental obligations relating to protected sites and species. Also reforms the NSIP regime, limits repeat judicial review of major infrastructure decisions, and amends provisions on environmental outcomes reports. [Themes: nature-based solutions; natural capital; ecosystem services]
Status: In force (Royal Assent 18 Dec 2025; phased commencement)

Name: Countryside and Rights of Way Act 2000 (CRoW Act)
Statutory_Enabling_Basis: Primary Act of Parliament — self-authorising. Section 2 grants open access rights; ss.28–33 strengthen SSSI protections; s.85 places duty on public bodies in National Parks and AONBs to have regard to purposes.
Key_Provisions: Provides right of open access to mountain, moor, heath, down, registered common land. Strengthens SSSI system. New powers for AONBs (now National Landscapes).

Name: Agriculture Act 2020
Statutory_Enabling_Basis: Primary Act of Parliament — self-authorising. Section 1 grants Ministers power to make financial assistance regulations for environmental purposes (ELM scheme secondary legislation made under this power).
Key_Provisions: Enables Environmental Land Management (ELM) schemes. Phases out EU Common Agricultural Policy (CAP) direct payments. Sets framework for paying farmers for delivering public goods including biodiversity and climate mitigation/adaptation.
Intl_Links: [EU-L-015] EU Common Agricultural Policy (CAP) — Strategic Plans Regulation (EU 2021/2115)

Name: Environmental Assessment of Plans and Programmes Regulations 2004
Statutory_Enabling_Basis: European Communities Act 1972 (now European Union (Withdrawal) Act 2018): regulations originally made to implement EU Strategic Environmental Assessment (SEA) Directive 2001/42/EC. Post-Brexit authority preserved as retained EU-derived law; obligations on Ministers and public bodies to assess plans and programmes.
Key_Provisions: Implements retained EU Strategic Environmental Assessment (SEA) Directive. Requires environmental assessment of certain plans/programmes that may have significant effects on the environment.

Name: Infrastructure Act 2015 (s.26 – carbon lock-in)
Statutory_Enabling_Basis: Primary Act of Parliament — self-authorising. Section 26 establishes the Oil and Gas Authority (now North Sea Transition Authority); interacts with net-zero via Carbon Budget obligations.
Key_Provisions: Includes provisions on maximising economic recovery of oil and gas. Amended by energy transition commitments; interacts with net-zero targets.

Name: Climate and Nature Bill (PMB)
Statutory_Enabling_Basis: Private Member's Bill — no statutory basis yet. If enacted would derive authority as primary legislation. Proposed to confer powers on SoS to make strategy and on CCC and JNCC to report on delivery.
Key_Provisions: Private Member's Bill (Roz Savage, Lib Dem). Would require UK to achieve integrated climate and nature targets aligned with Paris Agreement and UNCBD GBF. Would create Climate and Nature Assembly. Assign duties to CCC and JNCC. 2nd reading adjourned Jan 2025; resumed debate due May 2026. Government agreed to deliver bill's 'spirit and substance' through other means.

Name: Marine Strategy Regulations 2010 (as amended)
Statutory_Enabling_Basis: European Communities Act 1972 (now retained EU law via European Union (Withdrawal) Act 2018, s.2): originally made to implement the EU Marine Strategy Framework Directive (2008/56/EC). Retained and amended post-Brexit. Statutory authority now preserved as assimilated EU-derived law.
Key_Provisions: Imposes a statutory duty on UK and devolved governments to develop and implement a UK Marine Strategy aimed at achieving Good Environmental Status (GES) in UK seas by 2020 (now rolling 6-year cycles). Covers 11 descriptors including biodiversity, food webs, seafloor integrity, contaminants, and marine litter. Requires assessment, objective-setting, monitoring programmes and programmes of measures. Underpins the UK Marine Strategy (UKMS) published under these Regulations.
Status: In force (as amended; 6-year cycle; 2025 programme of measures published)
Intl_Links: [INT-L-013] OSPAR Convention for the Protection of the Marine Environment of the North-East Atlantic; [INT-L-017] Helsinki Convention (HELCOM) — Baltic Marine Environment Protection Convention; [INT-O-008] OSPAR Commission; [INT-O-009] International Council for the Exploration of the Sea; [INT-P-012] OSPAR North-East Atlantic Environment Strategy 2030 (NEAES 2030); [EU-L-004] EU Marine Strategy Framework Directive (Directive 2008/56/EC — MSFD); [EU-L-018] EU Single-Use Plastics Directive (Directive EU 2019/904)

Name: Water Act 2014
Statutory_Enabling_Basis: Primary Act of Parliament — self-authorising.
Key_Provisions: Amends water company licensing; introduces resilience duties; reforms abstraction licensing; enables Ofwat to set outcome-based price controls (PR19 onwards).

Name: Environment Act 1995
Statutory_Enabling_Basis: Primary Act of Parliament — self-authorising.
Key_Provisions: Established the Environment Agency (England & Wales) and SEPA. Sets duties for integrated pollution control, waste regulation, and flood risk management.

Name: Water Resources Act 1991
Statutory_Enabling_Basis: Primary Act of Parliament — self-authorising.
Key_Provisions: Grants EA powers over water abstraction licensing, flood risk, and water quality. Defines controlled waters and regulates discharge consents.

Name: Environmental Permitting (England and Wales) Regulations 2016
Statutory_Enabling_Basis: Made under Environment Act 1995 and various enabling Acts; SI 2016/1154.
Key_Provisions: Consolidated permitting regime for installations, waste operations, water discharge, flood risk activities, and radioactive substances. Administered by the EA.

Name: Forestry Act 1967
Statutory_Enabling_Basis: Primary Act of Parliament — self-authorising.
Key_Provisions: Established the Forestry Commission and its functions. Provides statutory basis for felling licences, restocking conditions, and forestry dedication agreements.

Name: Gas Act 1986
Statutory_Enabling_Basis: Primary Act of Parliament — self-authorising.
Key_Provisions: Liberalised the UK gas market. Grants Ofgem (through the Gas and Electricity Markets Authority) powers to licence gas transporters, suppliers, and interconnectors.

Name: Utilities Act 2000
Statutory_Enabling_Basis: Primary Act of Parliament — self-authorising.
Key_Provisions: Created Ofgem and the Gas and Electricity Markets Authority. Introduced social and environmental obligations on energy suppliers. Amended the Gas Act 1986 and Electricity Act 1989.

Name: Greenhouse Gas Emissions Trading Scheme Order 2020 (SI 2020/1265)
Statutory_Enabling_Basis: Made under the Finance Act 2020 and European Union (Withdrawal) Act 2018; SI 2020/1265.
Key_Provisions: Established the UK Emissions Trading Scheme (UK ETS) post-Brexit. Sets a cap on GHG emissions from covered sectors (power, industry, aviation). Expanded by Energy Act 2023.
Intl_Links: [EU-L-014] EU Emissions Trading System (Directive 2003/87/EC, as amended by Directive EU 2023/959)

Name: Finance Act 2020
Statutory_Enabling_Basis: Primary Act of Parliament — self-authorising.
Key_Provisions: Schedule 7 provides penalty and enforcement powers underpinning the UK ETS. Also covers taxation provisions relevant to energy and carbon pricing.

Name: Nature Conservation (Scotland) Act 2004
Statutory_Enabling_Basis: Primary Act of the Scottish Parliament — self-authorising.
Key_Provisions: Strengthened SSSI protection in Scotland. Placed a biodiversity duty on Scottish public bodies. Established the Scottish Biodiversity Strategy and NatureScot advisory role.

Name: Wildlife and Natural Environment (Scotland) Act 2011
Statutory_Enabling_Basis: Primary Act of the Scottish Parliament — self-authorising.
Key_Provisions: Amended wildlife crime provisions; updated deer management; reformed invasive species controls; strengthened protection for Schedule 1 species in Scotland.

Name: UK Withdrawal from the European Union (Continuity) (Scotland) Act 2021
Statutory_Enabling_Basis: Primary Act of the Scottish Parliament (2021 asp 4) — self-authorising.
Key_Provisions: Part 2 Chapter 1 imposes a duty on Scottish Ministers and other authorities to have due regard to the guiding environmental principles; Part 2 Chapter 2 (s.19) establishes Environmental Standards Scotland [ORG-045] to scrutinise compliance with and the effectiveness of environmental law. Part 1 gives Ministers powers to keep Scots law aligned with EU law. Repurposed in v27 from a non-existent 'Environment (Scotland) Act 2023' record whose provisions described this Act; ID kept so inbound references stay intact.

Name: Environment (Wales) Act 2016
Statutory_Enabling_Basis: Primary Act of the Senedd Cymru — self-authorising.
Key_Provisions: Sets a statutory biodiversity and resilience of ecosystems duty on Welsh public authorities. Requires NRW to publish State of Natural Resources Reports (SoNaRR) and area statements.

Name: Well-being of Future Generations (Wales) Act 2015
Statutory_Enabling_Basis: Primary Act of the Senedd Cymru — self-authorising.
Key_Provisions: Requires Welsh public bodies to consider seven long-term well-being goals including climate resilience and biodiversity. Established the Future Generations Commissioner for Wales.

Name: Natural Resources Body for Wales (Establishment) Order 2012
Statutory_Enabling_Basis: Made under the Public Bodies Act 2011.
Key_Provisions: Established Natural Resources Wales by merging Countryside Council for Wales, Environment Agency Wales, and Forestry Commission Wales.

Name: Environment (Northern Ireland) Order 2002
Statutory_Enabling_Basis: Order in Council — primary legislation equivalent; self-authorising.
Key_Provisions: Primary environmental framework for Northern Ireland. Grants NIEA powers over pollution control, waste regulation, and nature conservation in NI.

Name: Wildlife (Northern Ireland) Order 1985
Statutory_Enabling_Basis: Order in Council — primary legislation equivalent; self-authorising.
Key_Provisions: Provides protection for wild birds, animals, and plants in Northern Ireland. Equivalent to the Wildlife and Countryside Act 1981 for the NI jurisdiction.

Name: Clean Air (Northern Ireland) Order 1981
Statutory_Enabling_Basis: Northern Ireland Order in Council (SI 1981/158 (N.I. 4)), made under the Northern Ireland Act 1974 — primary legislation for Northern Ireland, self-authorising.
Key_Provisions: Northern Ireland's clean air law: prohibits dark smoke from chimneys and industrial premises; requires smokeless furnaces and grit and dust arrestment; controls chimney heights; provides for smoke control areas and smoke nuisance abatement, enforced by district councils. Carries transitional provisions and repeals relating to the Clean Air Act (Northern Ireland) 1964, which it replaced. NI counterpart of [LEG-062] Clean Air Act 1993. Repurposed in v28: the record previously named the 1964 Act but its Link opened the Petroleum (Production) Act (Northern Ireland) 1964.

Name: National Heritage Act 1983
Statutory_Enabling_Basis: Primary Act of Parliament — self-authorising.
Key_Provisions: Established the Royal Botanic Gardens, Kew as an Executive NDPB with exempt charitable status. Also covers the National Heritage Memorial Fund and other heritage bodies.

Name: Animal Health Act 1981
Statutory_Enabling_Basis: Primary Act of Parliament — self-authorising.
Key_Provisions: Provides powers for controlling animal disease outbreaks including slaughter, movement controls, and vaccination. Primary enabling Act for APHA's animal health functions.
Intl_Links: [INT-O-029] World Organisation for Animal Health (formerly OIE)

Name: Plant Health Act 1967
Statutory_Enabling_Basis: Primary Act of Parliament — self-authorising.
Key_Provisions: Enables controls on import, movement, and destruction of plants to prevent pest and disease spread. Primary enabling Act for Plant Health Orders (England, Scotland, Wales).

Name: Plant Health (England) Order 2015 (SI 2015/610)
Statutory_Enabling_Basis: Made under the Plant Health Act 1967; SI 2015/610.
Key_Provisions: Implements plant health requirements in England. Controls import, movement, and inspection of regulated plants and plant products. Delivered through APHA.

Name: Plant Health (Scotland) Order 2005
Statutory_Enabling_Basis: Made under the Plant Health Act 1967.
Key_Provisions: Scottish equivalent of the Plant Health (England) Order. Controls plant pest and disease movement in Scotland. Delivered through Scottish Forestry and APHA.

Name: Aquatic Animal Health (England and Wales) Regulations 2009
Statutory_Enabling_Basis: Made under the European Communities Act 1972 (retained); SI 2009/463.
Key_Provisions: Implements controls on aquatic animal diseases in fish, molluscs, and crustaceans. Cefas is the competent authority for disease surveillance and movement controls.
Intl_Links: [INT-O-029] World Organisation for Animal Health (formerly OIE)

Name: Water Framework Directive (retained UK law)
Statutory_Enabling_Basis: Retained from EU Directive 2000/60/EC under the European Union (Withdrawal) Act 2018.
Key_Provisions: Requires good ecological and chemical status for all water bodies. Sets river basin management planning cycles. Administered by EA, SEPA, NRW, and NIEA.
Intl_Links: [EU-L-003] EU Water Framework Directive (Directive 2000/60/EC); [EU-L-011] EU Nitrates Directive (Council Directive 91/676/EEC); [EU-L-012] EU Floods Directive (Directive 2007/60/EC); [EU-L-016] EU Groundwater Directive (Directive 2006/118/EC)

Name: Meteorological Office Trading Fund Order 1996 (SI 1996/774)
Statutory_Enabling_Basis: Made under the Government Trading Funds Act 1973; SI 1996/774.
Key_Provisions: Established the Met Office as a trading fund, enabling it to operate on a commercial basis as an executive agency of DESNZ.

Name: Government Trading Funds Act 1973
Statutory_Enabling_Basis: Primary Act of Parliament — self-authorising.
Key_Provisions: Enables government departments and agencies to operate as ring-fenced trading funds. Statutory basis for the Meteorological Office Trading Fund Order 1996.

Name: Energy Act 2010
Statutory_Enabling_Basis: Primary Act of Parliament — self-authorising.
Key_Provisions: Provides powers for the Boiler Upgrade Scheme (Clean Heat Grant). Includes provisions on energy efficiency obligations, fuel poverty reporting, and mandatory carbon reporting.

Name: Energy Act 2013
Statutory_Enabling_Basis: Primary Act of Parliament — self-authorising.
Key_Provisions: Established Contracts for Difference (CfD) as the primary low-carbon electricity support mechanism. Created the Capacity Market. Established the Office for Nuclear Regulation.

Name: Fisheries Act 2020
Statutory_Enabling_Basis: Primary Act of Parliament — self-authorising.
Key_Provisions: Post-Brexit fisheries management framework. Sets objectives including sustainability, equal access, and national benefit. Replaced the Common Fisheries Policy for UK waters.

Name: Town and Country Planning Act 1990
Policy_Sector: Nature & Biodiversity | Urban & Buildings | Land Use & Agriculture
Statutory_Enabling_Basis: Primary Act of Parliament — self-authorising.
Key_Provisions: Principal planning statute. Governs development control, planning permissions, and planning obligations (s.106). Statutory basis for nutrient neutrality planning conditions.

Name: Planning Act 2008
Policy_Sector: Energy | Climate | Nature & Biodiversity | Urban & Buildings | Land Use & Agriculture
Statutory_Enabling_Basis: Establishes the Nationally Significant Infrastructure Project (NSIP) consenting regime and the National Policy Statements (NPS) that set policy for development consent.
Key_Provisions: Creates the development consent order (DCO) regime for nationally significant infrastructure (energy generation incl. offshore wind, grid, transport, water). Requires designation of National Policy Statements (e.g. EN-1 overarching energy NPS, updated 2024) against which applications are examined. Primary consenting route at the energy-nature interface; interacts with Habitats Regulations assessment and (in future) Environmental Outcomes Reports.

Name: Levelling-up and Regeneration Act 2023
Policy_Sector: Nature & Biodiversity | Land Use & Agriculture | Governance, Society & Data
Statutory_Enabling_Basis: Part 6 confers powers to set environmental outcomes and require Environmental Outcomes Reports (EORs); also provides for nutrient pollution standards and provisions on National Parks, National Landscapes (AONBs) and the Broads.
Key_Provisions: Part 6 introduces Environmental Outcomes Reports (EORs) to replace the EU-derived EIA and SEA regimes; EORs must have regard to the Environmental Improvement Plan (England) / national natural resources policy (Wales). Government roadmap (2026) aims to bring EORs forward by end of 2027. Also reforms plan-making, introduces National Development Management Policies, and addresses nutrient neutrality.

Name: Retained EU Law (Revocation and Reform) Act 2023
Statutory_Enabling_Basis: Provides for the revocation, restatement, replacement and amendment of retained / assimilated EU law and removes EU supremacy and general principles from domestic law.
Key_Provisions: Sits upstream of much UK environmental law of EU origin (Habitats and Species Regulations, Water Framework Directive provisions, environmental assessment). Renamed retained EU law as assimilated law from end-2023 and removed EU interpretive principles, with powers to amend or replace via secondary legislation. Material to the durability and interpretation of several records in this sheet.

Name: Town and Country Planning (Environmental Impact Assessment) Regulations 2017 (SI 2017/571)
Policy_Sector: Nature & Biodiversity | Urban & Buildings | Land Use & Agriculture
Statutory_Enabling_Basis: Made under the Town and Country Planning Act 1990 (and formerly the European Communities Act 1972); transposes project-level environmental impact assessment for town-and-country planning consents.
Key_Provisions: Requires environmental impact assessment of specified development likely to have significant environmental effects, including effects on biodiversity, land, soil, water, air and climate. Project-level counterpart to the plan/programme SEA regime [LEG-019]; to be replaced by Environmental Outcomes Reports under [LEG-055].

Name: Climate Change (Scotland) Act 2009
Statutory_Enabling_Basis: Devolved Scottish climate framework legislation setting emissions reduction targets and a duty to publish climate change plans.
Key_Provisions: Sets a net-zero greenhouse gas emissions target for Scotland by 2045 (as amended 2019), with interim targets, and requires Scottish climate change plans. The Scottish devolved counterpart to the UK Climate Change Act 2008; the Climate Change Committee advises Scottish Ministers.

Name: Climate Change Act (Northern Ireland) 2022
Statutory_Enabling_Basis: Devolved Northern Ireland climate framework legislation setting emissions targets, carbon budgets and oversight bodies.
Key_Provisions: Sets a net-zero greenhouse gas emissions target for Northern Ireland by 2050 with at least a 48% reduction by 2030, a carbon-budgeting framework (first budgets 2023-27, 2028-32, 2033-37), sectoral plans and Climate Action Plans, and establishes the Northern Ireland Climate Commissioner and a Just Transition Commission. NI devolved counterpart to the UK Climate Change Act 2008; CCC advises.

Name: Flood and Water Management Act 2010
Statutory_Enabling_Basis: Confers flood and coastal erosion risk management duties and powers; provides for the national FCERM strategy and lead local flood authorities.
Key_Provisions: Establishes the Environment Agency strategic overview of flood and coastal erosion risk management and the duty to produce a national FCERM strategy; creates lead local flood authorities for local flood risk; provides for sustainable drainage (SuDS). Central statutory basis for climate adaptation and catchment-scale nature-based flood management. [Themes: nature-based solutions; natural capital; ecosystem services]

Name: National Parks and Access to the Countryside Act 1949
Statutory_Enabling_Basis: Foundational protected-areas legislation creating National Parks, National Landscapes (formerly AONBs), National Nature Reserves and the basis for Sites of Special Scientific Interest.
Key_Provisions: Establishes National Parks and the designation of Areas of Outstanding Natural Beauty (now National Landscapes), National Nature Reserves, and (with the Wildlife and Countryside Act 1981) the SSSI series. Foundational to the protected-area network underpinning 30x30 commitments and ecosystem conservation. [Themes: nature-based solutions; natural capital; ecosystem services]

Name: Clean Air Act 1993
Statutory_Enabling_Basis: Consolidating clean-air legislation controlling smoke, grit, dust and fumes and providing for smoke control areas.
Key_Provisions: Controls emissions of smoke, grit and dust and provides for smoke control areas. Relevant to nature via nitrogen and ammonia deposition on designated habitats and to the air-quality dimension of climate policy. GB counterpart to the Clean Air Act (Northern Ireland) 1964.

Name: United Kingdom Internal Market Act 2020
Policy_Sector: Finance | Governance, Society & Data | Nature & Biodiversity
Statutory_Enabling_Basis: Establishes market-access principles (mutual recognition and non-discrimination) for goods and services across the four UK nations after EU exit.
Key_Provisions: Sets mutual-recognition and non-discrimination principles for the UK internal market, constraining how far devolved environmental and product standards can diverge in practice. Governance-level context for divergence in climate and nature regulation across England, Scotland, Wales and Northern Ireland.

Name: Energy Act 2008
Statutory_Enabling_Basis: Provides for offshore gas and carbon dioxide storage licensing, feed-in tariffs and renewable/low-carbon electricity support.
Key_Provisions: Created powers for feed-in tariffs and the renewable heat incentive framework, and the licensing regime for offshore carbon dioxide and gas storage (relevant to CCUS). Earliest of the modern Energy Acts (preceding the 2010, 2013 and 2023 Acts already in this sheet).

Name: Land Drainage Act 1991
Statutory_Enabling_Basis: Consolidating legislation governing internal drainage boards and land drainage functions.
Key_Provisions: Sets the functions of internal drainage boards and local authorities for land drainage and ordinary watercourses. Relevant to catchment water management, lowland peat and wetland hydrology, and works alongside the Flood and Water Management Act 2010 and Water Resources Act 1991.

Name: Agriculture (Wales) Act 2023
Policy_Sector: Land Use & Agriculture | Nature & Biodiversity | Climate
Statutory_Enabling_Basis: Primary Act of Senedd Cymru — self-authorising. Establishes Sustainable Land Management (SLM) as the legislative framework for Welsh agricultural policy and the power to provide support (basis for the Sustainable Farming Scheme). Replaces the time-limited Welsh powers in Schedule 5 of the Agriculture Act 2020.
Key_Provisions: Establishes Sustainable Land Management as the statutory framework for Welsh agriculture and the powers to fund the Sustainable Farming Scheme [POL-056]; allows continued support payments during transition. Amends the Forestry Act 1967 (felling-licence conditions for NRW) and the Agricultural Holdings Act 1986 (tenant dispute resolution). Bans the use of snares and glue traps — a UK first.

Name: Agriculture and Rural Communities (Scotland) Act 2024
Policy_Sector: Land Use & Agriculture | Nature & Biodiversity | Climate
Statutory_Enabling_Basis: Primary Act of the Scottish Parliament — self-authorising. Framework Act conferring powers on Scottish Ministers to provide agricultural and rural support (basis for the Agricultural Reform Programme). Royal Assent 30 July 2024; key support powers commenced 16 June 2025 (S.S.I. 2025/167).
Key_Provisions: Framework enabling Scotland’s future agricultural support replacing CAP-era payments (the Agricultural Reform Programme, [POL-057]). Requires a Rural Support Plan; objectives include climate-change adaptation and mitigation, nature restoration, food production and resilient rural communities, with regard to the Climate Change (Scotland) Act 2009 climate change plan and the Good Food Nation (Scotland) Act 2022. Provides powers for support, conditionality and continuation of CAP-era schemes during transition.
Status: In force (key provisions commenced 16 Jun 2025; phased)

Name: Natural Environment (Scotland) Act 2026
Policy_Sector: Nature & Biodiversity | Land Use & Agriculture | Marine & Fisheries
Statutory_Enabling_Basis: Primary Act of the Scottish Parliament (2026 asp 6) — self-authorising.
Key_Provisions: Part 1 requires Scottish Ministers to set statutory targets for improving biodiversity (habitat condition, species status and environmental conditions) with accompanying monitoring and compliance reporting; Environmental Standards Scotland [ORG-045] has an independent assurance role. Part 2 amends National Park aims, adds national park policy statements, a duty on public bodies to facilitate implementation of park plans, and fixed-penalty byelaw enforcement. Part 3 reforms deer management (revised aims, code of practice, management plans and control schemes, NatureScot investigatory powers). Part 4 covers swift nest boxes in new buildings, climate adaptation for marine protected areas, salmon and freshwater fishing offences, gull reporting, wildlife licensing, wildfire, forestry and muirburn licensing. The biodiversity targets and their indicators are not yet set; when published they are IFW and IND candidates.
Status: Royal Assent 12 Mar 2026 (commencement phased, incl. SSI 2026/275)

Name: Environment (Principles, Governance and Biodiversity Targets) (Wales) Act 2026
Statutory_Enabling_Basis: Act of Senedd Cymru (2026 asc 4) — self-authorising.
Key_Provisions: Part 1 sets an environmental objective and environmental principles that Welsh Ministers, Natural Resources Wales [ORG-015] and other public authorities must apply, with integration statements. Part 2 establishes the Office of Environmental Governance Wales [ORG-046] (strategy, monitoring of environmental law, advice, information notices, investigations, compliance notices, improvement reports). Part 3 amends the Environment (Wales) Act 2016 [LEG-035] to create a framework of statutory biodiversity targets aimed at halting and reversing biodiversity decline, with progress reporting. Targets not yet set.
Status: In force (phased commencement: most of Parts 1–3 from 27 Jun 2026; ss.3–5 from 31 Mar 2027; remainder by order)

Name: Building Act 1984
Statutory_Enabling_Basis: Primary Act of Parliament (1984 c. 55) — self-authorising.
Key_Provisions: Section 1 and Schedule 1 empower the making of building regulations (the Building Regulations 2010 and their Parts, including Part O overheating [POL-074] and Part L energy efficiency). Extensively amended, including by the Building Safety Act 2022 (higher-risk buildings, Building Safety Regulator). Held as the enabling legislation for building-standard policy records.

Name: The Northern Ireland Climate Commissioner Regulations (Northern Ireland) 2025 (SR 2025 No. 78)
Statutory_Enabling_Basis: Made under section 50 of the Climate Change Act (Northern Ireland) 2022 [LEG-059].
Key_Provisions: Establishes the office of the Northern Ireland Climate Commissioner [ORG-031] and sets its functions and general powers, appointment and tenure, staffing, finance, accounts and annual reporting.
Status: In force (made 8 Apr 2025; in operation 9 Apr 2025)
